title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck tries to axiomatize an 'atelier' (workshop), a combinatorial or synthetic model of geometric figures and places. Its data are a set M of figures with three relations: an order ≤, an auxiliary relation ≪ (with a strict or 'interior' variant ˚≪), and a disjointness or separation relation ≭. There is also a set L of minimal elements (lieux/points) carrying a parallelism or 'ligature' relation ∥. On p.38 he showed that, starting from (M, ≤, ≪), the possible ∥ on L can be any symmetric Γ with Γ0 ⊂ Γ ⊂ P2(L).

On p.39 he observes that the earlier argument used the minimality of the elements of L only at the very end. That step was needed to show that ∥ on L is the relation induced by the disposition of the places in the reconstructed atelier. He therefore restarts the theory with an arbitrary 'dense' subset Λ ⊂ M in place of L.

Definition: Λ is dense (in M) if for every X ∈ M there is Y ∈ Λ with Y ˚≪ X. Examples: Λ = M is the 'universal' case (take Y = X, so ˚≪ is reflexive). Λ = L is dense when axiom At L1 holds.

Programme: give axioms on the structure (M, ≤, ≪, ≭, Λ ⊂ M) that guarantee two things. First, that (M, ≤, ≪, ≭) comes from an atelier. Second, that Λ is dense, possibly with an extra condition on the atelier (At D, At D0 or At C). This is a representation theorem 'from below', reconstructing the space from a dense family of elements.

The axioms:
- MΛ0 ('trivial'): X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪ Y, so ≪ extends ≤.
- MΛ1 ('sufficiency / induction', heavily corrected): suppose Y ≪ X, Z ∈ Λ with Z ≪ Y and Z ≪ X, and X' (apparently X' ≤ X, given the vertical ≤ drawn under X). Then there is Y' ≤ Y with Y' ≪ X' and Z ≪ Y'. Moreover, if Y ≤ X then Y' ≤ X'. In other words, ≪ restricts along ≤ while keeping a witnessing element of Λ.
- MΛ2 (density): every X has some Z ∈ Λ with Z ˚≪ X.
- MΛ3 ('minimal ...'): if Z ∈ Λ and Z ≪ X, there is X' ≤ X with Z ˚≪ X'.

He then introduces the 'shadows' of X on Λ: omb_Λ(X) = {Z ∈ Λ | Z ≪ X} and omb_Λ(X)° = {Z ∈ Λ | Z ˚≪ X}. He announces that the previous arguments (pp. 25–28) give lemmas expressing ≤ and ≪ through inclusions and non-empty intersections of shadows. These are stated on p.40 as Lemmas A, B, C and a corollary.

The point of the whole construction is a Stone-type or 'points-from-regions' reconstruction: elements of M are recovered through their traces on a dense subfamily Λ.
errors: MΛ1 is left in a heavily corrected, incomplete state. The roles of Y and Z were swapped mid-writing (Z' ≤ Z crossed out, replaced by Y' ≤ Y). The hypothesis on X' is not stated in words; presumably X' ≤ X and Z ≪ X', since otherwise the conclusion Z ≪ Y' ≪ X' would force Z ≪ X' anyway. As written, the axiom is not fully well-formed.
The page announces 'deux lemmes ci-dessous', but p.40 gives three lemmas (A, B, C) plus a corollary. This is a minor inconsistency.
The definition of 'dense' and axiom MΛ2 are literally the same statement. This is redundant, but the redundancy is intended: the axiom builds density into the abstract structure.

The meaning of ≪ and ˚≪ cannot be fully determined from this page. MΛ0 (≤ ⇒ ≪) shows that ≪ is coarser than ≤, which is the opposite of the 'well-inside' relation of mereotopology. Any identification with modern notions is therefore tentative.

ideas.what: Replacing the set of minimal places L by an arbitrary dense subfamily Λ ⊂ M, and axiomatizing when (M, ≤, ≪, ≭, Λ) comes from an atelier with Λ dense.
ideas.modern_name: Representation theorem via a dense basis; analogous to dense subsets / bases in point-free topology and to representation of region-based contact structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936), Tarski (geometry of solids, 1929); for contact algebras de Vries (1962), Dimov–Vakarelov (2006)
ideas.where_published: Only the general 'tame topology' programme is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the atelier axiomatics appears unpublished

ideas.what: Shadows omb_Λ(X) and omb_Λ(X)°: the traces of a figure on the dense family, used to characterize ≤ and ≪ by inclusion and intersection of shadows.
ideas.modern_name: Trace / 'shadow' map M → P(Λ) (Stone-type embedding into a powerset; separation by a dense subfamily)

ideas.what: The density notion (∀X ∃Y∈Λ, Y ˚≪ X) with examples Λ = M and Λ = L under At L1.
ideas.modern_name: Dense subset of a poset or relational structure

missed.claim: The 1986 atelier axiomatics, with its relations ≤, ≪ (˚≪), ≭ and representation via shadows on a dense subfamily, is structurally a region-based synthetic topology/geometry. It parallels mereotopology and contact algebras (Whitehead, de Laguna, Tarski; Düntsch, Vakarelov, Dimov). No literature connecting Grothendieck's 'analysis situs' ateliers to that tradition is known to me.
missed.quote: On va donner des axiomes sur (M, ≤, ≪, ≭, Λ ⊂ M) qui assurent que (M, ≤, ≪, ≭) provient d'un atelier, et que Λ ⊂ M est dense
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It situates Grothendieck's tame-topology/analysis situs programme within existing representation theory for region-based spaces. That could make the unpublished chapters intelligible and comparable to known results.

missed.claim: Axiom MΛ1 is left in a provisional, heavily corrected form, and the whole Λ-version of the reconstruction is only begun here. It is unclear whether a clean axiom system with a proved representation theorem was ever reached.
missed.quote: M Λ 1  si Y ≪ X et Z ∈ Λ tel que Z ≪ Y, Z ≪ X; X', alors ∃Y' tel que Y' ≤ Y, Y' ≪ X', Z ≪ Y'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Completing the axiomatics would give a precise statement of Grothendieck's intended combinatorial model for figures and places. That is relevant to o-minimal / tame-topology foundations.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical restart of an unpublished axiomatic construction (a dense subfamily replacing minimal points, plus shadow maps). It is interesting as documentation of the analysis situs programme, but the techniques are standard Stone-type representation ideas and the page contains no completed new result.

In MΛ1 a vertical '≤' is written below X, indicating X' ≤ X as the hypothesis on X'. 'Z ≤ X' in the last line is crossed out and replaced by 'Y ≤ X'; the conclusion is 'alors Y' ≤ X''.
Margin by MΛ3 reads roughly 'Axiome de la limite/finitude minimale' (uncertain). Margin by MΛ2 reads 'Axiome de densité' followed by a crossed-out word.
Bottom-left oblique margin: roughly 'Pour le moment il s'agit des axiomes pour [≭?] ... [?]' (uncertain).
A crossed-out bracketed annotation in the right margin spans MΛ0–MΛ1 and is not transcribed.
